title: KinetiQ E1 — verbatim-extraction measurement-accuracy benchmark harness and per-repetition outputs
description: Benchmark harness, extracted measurement core, per-repetition outputs and figure scripts supporting the manuscript "Benchmarking the Deployed Artifact: Verbatim-Extraction Testing and Viewing-Angle Error Decomposition of a Browser-Based Markerless Movement Assessment Platform" (submitted to IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics). The harness slices the measurement functions of a deployed single-page web application from its shipped source by line range, records a SHA-256 for each, and executes them unmodified against three reference tiers (analytic synthetic kinematics; motion-capture trajectories injected at the landmark interface, REHAB24-6 and UI-PRMD; and end-to-end video through the production MediaPipe configuration). From v1.0.2 the pose estimator is version-pinned in both the application and the harness (@mediapipe/pose 0.5.1675469404) with per-asset SHA-256 recorded in harness/pose_assets.json, and verify_pose_assets.cjs checks that the pinned and previously-unversioned CDN paths serve byte-identical assets. tier2_reference_3d.py rescores the Tier 2 outputs against a 3-D anatomical reference so the literature comparison can be read against either reference convention. v1.0.3 adds sts_verify.cjs --core/--sts/--out, which replays a pre-fix build so that the "before" column of the paper's defect table is reproducible from the archive rather than asserted; results/sts_report_precorrection.json is the output. v1.0.4 adds ICC(2,1) (two-way random effects, absolute agreement, single measurement) to tier2_stats.cjs and its archived output, matching the manuscript's reported ICC of 0.93 sagittal and 0.18 oblique; all previously published values are unchanged. Raw datasets are not redistributed here: REHAB24-6 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.13305826, CC BY-NC 4.0) and UI-PRMD (University of Idaho, ODC-PDDL v1.0) must be obtained from their original sources. v1.0.5 fixes clipped 0-deg and 90-deg data markers in the viewing-angle figure script (the axis limits coincided with the data endpoints); figure script only, no number changes.
